title: Velocity Systems - Implementation Kickoff & Onboarding Workshop
summary: Kickoff for Velocity Systems' Redwood Inference onboarding. Covered high-level rollout plan, environment options (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC), security requirements (SOC2, KMS, audit logs), success criteria, initial pilot scope, and next steps to provision test capacity. SE walked through runway for a two-week pilot with perf benchmarks and integration checkpoints. Action items captured for provisioning, security docs, and sample prompts/traffic profile.
topics: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
Security: SOC 2, SSO, KMS, data residency
Observability and cost controls (Console, token breakdown, batching)
action_items: Maya Chen - Provide sample traffic profile and top 50 prompt templates by 2026-03-26
Diego Martinez (Redwood) - Share onboarding runbook + security pack (SOC2, ISO) by 2026-03-23
Priya Reddy (Redwood SE) - Schedule perf benchmark window and initial model configs by 2026-03-25
Rashid Alvi - Confirm KMS provider details and VPN connectivity constraints by 2026-03-24
next_steps: Redwood to provision a 2-week Dedicated pilot (estimate configs) and share cost sheet
Customer to send traffic pattern + sample prompts
Security sync to review KMS/keys and audit log retention
Book perf run and demo of Console live telemetry
transcript:
[00:00] Sara Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll give folks another minute, but wanted to kick off, I'm Sara Kim from Redwood, AE on the account. Diego and Priya with me.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: Hey Sara, thanks. We got the invite. We're excited to get this going — short on time but high priority for us.
[00:30] Diego Martinez: Quick agenda, we'll do intros, success criteria, security checklist, pilot scoping, and then next steps. Priya will take the technical run.
[00:45] Tom Becker: Quick note, we care about latency — 95th percentile under 200ms for short completions if possible, and data can't leave EU region for this pilot.
[01:12] Priya Reddy: Got it, thanks Tom. The two levers there are Dedicated in eu-west or a Private VPC; for strict data residency Private is the safer route but Dedicated can be isolated depending on contract.
[01:40] Maya Chen: We also have throughput spikes. Peak qps can reach 120 rps for a bursty window, average around 18. Looking for autoscale behavior.
[02:05] Priya Reddy: That's helpful, Maya. Redwood Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst capacity. For the pilot we can set a burst cap and observe. We'll probably recommend continuous batching to improve token cost without hurting latency.
[02:32] Rashid Alvi: On security, SOC 2 reports are table stakes. Also need SSO/SAML integration, and we use HashiCorp Vault for keys, so KMS handshake and key rotation matter.
[02:55] Diego Martinez: We'll include SOC2 artifacts in the pack. We support KMS integrations and can work with Vault-based flow. We'll need network egress details for the VPC setup.
[03:20] Sara Kim: For clarity, this kickoff is to scope the 2-week pilot: canonical success is validated latency and cost per effective token below your target, and integration with your infra for routing and auth. Anything to add?
[03:45] Tom Becker: Also need to validate the Console telemetry — token breakdown per route, error rates, and a trace view.
[04:05] Priya Reddy: We'll demo the Console live later in the pilot. It shows per-model latency, per-route cost, and token-level billing.
[04:25] Liam O'Connor: On model choice, are you recommending an open model or Redwood-curated one? We prefer a smaller embedding model for retrieval and a medium LLM for generation.
[04:50] Priya Reddy: We'll propose model variants. For cost/perf we usually suggest trying a quantized 8-bit variant for the gen model and a production embeddings model from our catalog. We can switch routing to cheaper variants if we hit cost SLOs.
[05:15] Maya Chen: Can you give an example of the rollout plan timeline?
[05:25] Diego Martinez: Sure — Week 0: provision pilot environment and security review. Week 1: ingest sample traffic and run perf benchmarks. Week 2: iterate on configs, roll demo to stakeholders, finalize SLOs and next procurement steps.
[05:50] Rashid Alvi: On audit logs retention — we need 12 months immutable logs for requests metadata. Is that supported?
[06:05] Priya Reddy: Yes, Redwood Console emits audit logs; retention depends on plan, but for Private we can configure longer retention and ship to your SIEM. We'll note that as a requirement.
[06:30] [08:00] Speaker 4: (mumbled) ...I heard 'KV cash' — do you mean KV cache? We've had issues with cache warm up on cold starts.
[08:12] Priya Reddy: Yes KV cache, sorry the auto transcript is ugly. We'll walk through cache warming strategies and prefix caching to reduce cold-start latency.
[08:35] Tom Becker: For the pilot, we want to run a deterministic benchmark with our top 20 prompts and 3 sequence-length buckets: short (<=64 tokens), medium (~256), long (~1024).
[09:02] Priya Reddy: Perfect. That aligns to our kernel selection and batching strategy. We'll need to know the concurrency distribution to pick the right kernel/instance type.
[09:28] Liam O'Connor: Regarding cost, can you provide a sample cost sheet upfront? We want a rough estimate to justify the Dedicated pilot to Finance.
[09:45] Diego Martinez: We'll send an estimate and a granular token breakdown. The Console will also show per-route cost once running. For the pilot estimate we'll include reserved baseline and burst pricing.
[10:10] Maya Chen: Integration-wise, we plan to use your JS SDK and have a microservice that will proxy requests. Any requirements?
[10:25] Priya Reddy: JS SDK is straightforward; we'll provide sample code for streaming responses and function/tool calling. Key thing is to instrument retries and idempotency for our generated tokens, and configure batching windows on the SDK side if desired.
[10:50] [12:05] Sara Kim: Quick poll: Are there any blockers from procurement/security to start the pilot this week?
[12:15] Rashid Alvi: I need the security pack, and legal will want to review data processing addendum — also need to know where logs persist.
[12:28] Diego Martinez: We'll surface the DPA and share the security pack in 48 hours. Also we can provide a temporary limited-scope data flow diagram.
[12:45] Tom Becker: We also want guardrails for hallucination. Can you integrate evals into the pipeline?
[13:00] Priya Reddy: Yes, Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring tied to prompt sets and evals; we can wire up automated regression alerts for your critical prompts, and tie them to a canary rollback.
[13:20] Maya Chen: Who on your side will be the day-to-day contact?
[13:28] Diego Martinez: Diego is the CSM day-to-day, Priya handles technical, and Sara coordinates procurement and billing.
[13:40] [15:00] Liam O'Connor: On the private deployment, what's the rough lead time for staging?
[15:08] Priya Reddy: Private stack provisioning depends on network and cert exchange, typically 2-4 weeks. For a pilot we recommend Dedicated in the EU region which can be provisioned in days.
[15:30] Rashid Alvi: We prefer Dedicated for speed, but we need assurance on key management and network isolation.
[15:45] Priya Reddy: We can do Dedicated with customer-managed VPC peering and KMS integration so keys never leave your control; we'll document the flow.
[16:02] Sara Kim: Let's walk through the proposed pilot metrics — Diego, take us through them.
[16:12] Diego Martinez: Sure. Primary metrics: 95p latency (target 200ms for short), per-token cost (target TBD from your finance), error rate under 0.5%, and telemetry completeness (Console shows per-route traces, tokens, and errors). Secondary metrics: cache hit rate, warm-start latency.
[16:40] Maya Chen: For example data retention, we want request bodies ephemeral but metadata logged. Can you redact PII and still provide audit trails?
[16:55] Priya Reddy: Yes we support configurable redaction at the routing layer; we can also ship hashed identifiers for tracing. We'll need to map fields to redact.
[17:15] [18:00] Tom Becker: Any limitations on model size for Dedicated? We might want to test a 70B param variant in the future.
[18:12] Priya Reddy: Dedicated supports large models but instance selection changes. For pilot we recommend medium family; we can test large models in a later phase with capacity planning.
[18:35] Liam O'Connor: Ok, timeline recap?
[18:40] Diego Martinez: Action items: Maya to send traffic and prompts by 3/26, Redwood will send security pack by 3/23, Priya to schedule perf runs by 3/25, Rashid to confirm KMS details by 3/24. We'll provision a Dedicated pilot and send cost estimate.
[19:05] Maya Chen: Sounds good. Also can we get a short doc on recommended prompt engineering and sampling configs?
[19:18] Priya Reddy: We'll include a one-pager with prompt best practices and sampling/top-k/top-p recommendations.
[19:30] [22:00] Sara Kim: Any other questions?
[22:10] Tom Becker: One ask — show us the Console with our telemetry and the routing policies in action. Can that be part of Week 2?
[22:25] Priya Reddy: Yes, Week 2 demo includes Console walkthrough with live telemetry and rollout policy simulation.
[22:40] Liam O'Connor: Great. We'll align internally and get the artifacts sent.
[22:50] Diego Martinez: I'll follow up with calendar invites for the perf run and send the security pack.
[23:05] Sara Kim: Thanks everyone. We'll capture this and send a recap. Meeting adjourned.
[23:15] (end of recording)
questions: Can Redwood support 12-month immutable audit log retention?
What's the fastest path to prove latency SLOs in EU region?
How does KMS integration work with HashiCorp Vault?
Can we configure redaction of PII while maintaining traceability?
